findings.reason: fr_rx() receives an attacker-supplied Frame Relay frame as .netif_rx handler (drivers/net/wan/hdlc_fr.c:1180). It validates only total length ('if (skb->len < 4 || fh->ea1 || !fh->ea2 || data[2] != FR_UI)' line 899; 'if (skb->len < 5)' line 963) and then uses skb_pull() as if it linearized: skb_pull(skb,4) at lines 949/957 and skb_pull(skb,5) at line 966 are unchecked (return ignored) and only decrement skb->len against the TOTAL length including frags/fraglist; no pskb_may_pull/linearize exists anywhere in hdlc_fr.c. Worse, line 940 'skb = skb_share_check(skb, GFP_ATOMIC);' may replace/free the original shared skb, after which the saved pointer from line 894 (u8 *data = skb->data; also struct fr_hdr *fh = (struct fr_hdr *)skb->data; line 893) is dereferenced at lines 946, 954, 962, 965, 977 (data[3]/data[4]) - a stale pointer over the old freed head, plus post-pull fr_snap_parse (lines 849-884) reads skb->data[0..4] that the len-only pull never guaranteed to be in the linear head. Counterevidence checked: skb_pull_inline (include/linux/skbuff.h:2655-2658) clamps to skb->len, so a pull itself cannot move skb->data past the valid range, and if the WAN device never delivers non-linear skbs (many HDLC drivers deliver freshly allocated linear buffers) the reads stay in-bounds; skb_share_check only reallocates when the head is shared (cloned).
findings.conclusion: fr_rx() uses unchecked skb_pull(4/5) as a linearizer after only skb->len checks and keeps dereferencing the data pointer saved before skb_share_check() (line 940), so a non-linear or shared received frame can cause a stale-head read and reads of bytes not in the linear head (medium confidence).

candidates.reason: Main finding: skb_share_check may free the original skb head while 'data' (saved at line 894) and fh (line 893) continue to be dereferenced at 946/954/962/965/977; combined with unchecked len-only skb_pull calls.

l2cap_recv_frame() does 'struct l2cap_hdr *lh = (void *) skb->data;' then unchecked skb_pull(skb, L2CAP_HDR_SIZE) at line 7766 and reads lh->cid/lh->len afterwards with only an implied len check ('if (len != skb->len)') at 7771; hci_acldata_packet() (net/bluetooth/hci_core.c:3849-3853) has the same pattern for HCI_ACL_HDR_SIZE. The pull validates only against skb->len, so if an HCI transport hands a non-linear skb these reads touch bytes outside the linear head; however the HCI core (hci_rx_work -> hci_acldata_packet) was not traced to the individual transport drivers to establish which ones can deliver frags, and no skb_share_check-style free occurs here, so this is a len-only linearizer hypothesis not yet confirmed.
candidates.conclusion: Verify whether any HCI transport driver (drivers/bluetooth/*) can hand a non-linear skb into hci_acldata_packet/l2cap_recv_frame; if yes, lh->cid/len reads after the unchecked skb_pull(L2CAP_HDR_SIZE) touch non-linear bytes.

candidates.reason: cmtp_recv_frame's unchecked skb_pull calls (lines 167/186/259) operate on skbs that cmtp_session() explicitly linearized first: 'if (!skb_linearize(skb)) cmtp_recv_frame(session, skb); else kfree_skb(skb);' at net/bluetooth/cmtp/core.c:297-300, so skb->data always covers skb->len.

x25_parse_address_block() re-validates linear presence before every read ('if (!pskb_may_pull(skb, 1))' line 91 and 'if (!pskb_may_pull(skb, needed))' line 100) before calling x25_addr_ntoa(skb->data,...) at line 107, and x25_rx_call_request (lines 974-991) likewise pskb_may_pull's before each skb->data read; the subsequent skb_pull calls are unchecked but are preceded by matching length validation.

pppoatm_push() checks 'if (skb->len < LLC_LEN || memcmp(skb->data, pppllc, LLC_LEN))' (lines 198-199) then unchecked skb_pull(skb, LLC_LEN) (line 201) and in the autodetect branch reads 6 bytes after only 'skb->len >= sizeof(pppllc)' (line 205). memcmp(skb->data,...) itself reads LLC_LEN bytes guaranteed only in the len sense, not linearly; ATM AAL5 skbs are normally allocated linear by the driver, which was not verified per-driver.
candidates.conclusion: Confirm whether ATM AAL5 receive skbs (net/atm/* and drivers/atm/*) can be non-linear; if so the memcmp(skb->data, pppllc, LLC_LEN) at net/atm/pppoatm.c:199 reads beyond the linear head.

candidates.reason: a2mp_chan_recv_cb() loop does 'hdr = (void *) skb->data;' (line 615), reads hdr->len, then 'skb_pull(skb, sizeof(*hdr));' (line 622) and keeps dereferencing the saved hdr ('if (len > skb->len || !hdr->ident)' line 625; 'switch (hdr->code)' line 631) and after the switch 'skb_pull(skb, le16_to_cpu(hdr->len))' at line 682; subhandlers also do 'skb_pull(skb, le16_to_cpu(hdr->len))' (lines 550/604) with the return ignored. The loop guard 'while (skb->len >= sizeof(*hdr))' validates only total length; if the A2MP channel skb is non-linear (A2MP runs over an L2CAP channel fed by hci_acldata_packet) the hdr reads after pull touch non-linear bytes and the stale hdr pointer is used after the head may have been reallocated by other paths - the L2CAP channel recv path was not traced end-to-end to settle non-linearity.
candidates.conclusion: Trace l2cap_data_channel->a2mp_chan_recv_cb skb delivery to decide whether the hdr pointer saved before 'skb_pull(skb, sizeof(*hdr))' (net/bluetooth/a2mp.c:622) can be non-linear or be invalidated before the hdr->code/hdr->ident reads at 625/631.

candidates.reason: nfc_llcp_recv_agf() pulls the 2-byte header and per-PDU lengths with only total-len guards ('if (skb->len <= LLCP_HEADER_SIZE)' line 1387; 'while (skb->len > LLCP_AGF_PDU_HEADER_SIZE)' line 1400; 'if (pdu_len < LLCP_HEADER_SIZE || pdu_len > skb->len)' line 1405) then reads skb->data[0]/[1] (line 1401) and copies pdu_len bytes via skb_put_data (line 1417) from skb->data - none of these linear guarantees hold if the RX skb is non-linear; NFC response skbs are usually freshly allocated by digital_skb_alloc()/nfc_alloc_recv_skb (linear by construction), but the analog/NCI target paths and per-driver skb construction were not exhaustively checked.
candidates.conclusion: Determine whether any NFC driver (net/nfc/nci, drivers/nfc/*) can deliver a non-linear skb to nfc_llcp_recv_agf; if yes the skb->data[0]<<8|skb->data[1] read at line 1401 is out of the linear head.

candidates.reason: ax25_rcv() checks no linear length at all: it calls ax25_addr_parse(skb->data, skb->len, ...) which returns NULL only if fewer than 14+digis TOTAL bytes exist, then does unchecked 'skb_pull(skb, ax25_addr_size(&dp));' (line 218) and afterwards reads *skb->data and skb->data[1] (lines 241-243, 248) and in the connected path ax25_decode() (net/ax25/ax25_subr.c:97-149) reads frame[0]/frame[1] with unchecked skb_pull(skb,2). No pskb_may_pull exists anywhere in net/ax25/. Whether AX.25 (KISS over SLIP/mkiss, baycom, etc.) receive skbs can be non-linear was not verified; mkiss typically assembles linear skbs, which would keep the reads in-bounds.
candidates.conclusion: Verify whether any AX.25-capable device (drivers/net/hamradio/mkiss, 6pack, yam, scc) can hand a non-linear skb to ax25_kiss_rcv; if yes, reads of skb->data[0]/[1] after the unchecked skb_pull at ax25_in.c:218 read non-linear bytes.

coverage_gaps: The ~1100 pull-family sites in drivers/net/ were enumerated but only pattern-sampled (hdlc_fr.c read in full); files such as drivers/net/ethernet receive offload helpers and drivers/net/wireless were not individually audited.

No runtime or KASAN reproduction was performed (read-only snapshot, no network): the fr_rx stale-data-pointer after skb_share_check and the non-linear reads are inferred from source structure, not observed.

Non-linearity preconditions were assessed structurally (which subsystems linearize before parsing) rather than by tracing each hardware driver's skb allocation path (HCI transports, ATM AAL5, NFC, hamradio).

The prescribed open template net/decnet/dn_nsp_in.c:130-158 (dn_process_ack) does not exist in snapshots/s01 (no net/decnet tree at all), so that exact shape could only be matched by analogy, not verified in place.

Assigned sites named in prior facts (net/decnet/*, net/phonet/pep.c) were excluded or out of scope by instruction; phonet pep_get_sb was confirmed present at net/phonet/pep.c:45-66 but deliberately not reported.
limitations: All conclusions rest on static reading of snapshots/s01 exact lines; snapshot revision is opaque, so line numbers are valid only for this supplied tree.

The primary fr_rx finding's stale-pointer half depends on the received skb being shared/cloned at skb_share_check() and its non-linear half on the FRAD driver delivering frags; many WAN drivers build fresh linear skbs, in which case the code is merely fragile, not exploitable.

The five unresolved candidates (l2cap/hci_acldata, pppoatm, a2mp, llcp_agf, ax25) could not be closed because each hinges on per-driver non-linearity that a source snapshot alone does not resolve without tracing every hardware path.

The coarse scanner's statement-continuation heuristic (up to 6 lines) may have misjoined a few multi-line calls, so a small number of false positives/negatives among the 416 flagged sites cannot be excluded.
